core: Major clinical professions and their credentials: physicians (MD vs DO), registered nurses, advanced practice registered nurses (NP/CRNA/CNM), physician assistants/associates, pharmacists, allied health technologists and technicians
Licensure and scope of practice as state-defined concepts
Hospital ownership types: nongovernment not-for-profit, investor-owned for-profit, government (state/local and federal)
Other organizational forms: physician group practices, community health centers/FQHCs, integrated delivery networks/systems, academic medical centers, accountable care organizations (ACOs)
Hospital governance: governing body (board), organized medical staff, executive administration (the three-legged stool)
supporting: Workforce size, entry education, and projected growth figures from BLS OOH (2024 data)
Medicare Conditions of Participation basis for the board-medical staff-CEO structure
outOfScope: In-depth description of care settings themselves (what a SNF, ED, or ambulatory surgery center is) — owned by 'Healthcare Delivery Settings'
Leadership theory and competencies — owned by 'Healthcare Leadership'
Staffing/workforce management operations: scheduling, nurse-to-patient ratios, recruitment and retention — owned by 'Staffing and Workforce Management'
Individualized clinical, licensing, billing, or benefits-eligibility advice

claims.claim: MD (Doctor of Medicine) and DO (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine) are the two physician degrees; both use the same methods of treatment including drugs and surgery, and DO training adds emphasis on the musculoskeletal system, preventive medicine, and whole-person care. All states require physicians to be licensed.
Physicians and surgeons held about 839,000 jobs in 2024 and enter through a doctoral or professional degree; employment is projected to grow 3 percent from 2024 to 2034.

Registered nurses enter through a bachelor's degree, associate degree, or diploma program and must be licensed by their state; they held about 3,391,000 jobs in 2024 (median pay $93,600 in May 2024), with 5 percent growth projected 2024-2034.

Advanced practice roles (nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners) require a master's degree, held about 382,700 jobs in 2024, and are projected to grow 35 percent from 2024 to 2034, much faster than average.
Physician assistants enter through a master's-level program, held about 162,700 jobs in 2024 (median $133,260, May 2024), with 20 percent growth projected 2024-2034.
Pharmacists enter through a doctoral or professional degree (PharmD) and held about 335,100 jobs in 2024 (median $137,480, May 2024), with 5 percent growth projected 2024-2034.
Medical and health services managers typically enter with a bachelor's degree, held about 616,200 jobs in 2024 (median $117,960, May 2024), with 23 percent growth projected 2024-2034.
Scope of practice and licensure are defined by state law; the specific activities a professional may perform (for example, whether a nurse practitioner may prescribe independently) vary by state.

Per AHA data from its 2024 annual survey, the U.S. had about 6,100 hospitals total and 5,121 community hospitals; of the community hospitals, 2,984 were nongovernment not-for-profit, 1,224 investor-owned (for-profit), and 913 state/local government; 210 hospitals were federal government.

Federally qualified health centers are funded under Section 330 of the Public Health Service Act to provide primary care in underserved areas on a sliding fee scale; their governing board must have 9 to 25 members, at least 51 percent of whom are patients served by the center.

An accountable care organization under the Medicare Shared Savings Program is a voluntary group of doctors, hospitals, and other providers who coordinate care for Medicare patients and may share in savings achieved while meeting quality targets.

Under 42 CFR 482.12, a hospital must have an effective governing body legally responsible for the conduct of the hospital that appoints medical staff members (after considering their recommendations), approves medical staff bylaws, and appoints a CEO responsible for managing the hospital; under 42 CFR 482.22 the hospital must have an organized medical staff operating under board-approved bylaws, composed of doctors of medicine or osteopathy, accountable to the board for the quality of medical care.

conflictingEvidence.issue: BLS reports physicians' and surgeons' median wage as 'equal to or greater than $239,200 per year,' the top of its wage scale, rather than a precise midpoint.
positions: A single median dollar figure could be stated
The value is top-coded and only a lower bound is published
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson does not cite a precise physician median wage; it uses employment counts and the MD/DO distinction instead, avoiding an inaccurate point figure.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft treated 'Healthcare Professionals And Organizations' as an abstract study concept with placeholder text ('a concept students use to organize information'). No factual content in the draft was usable; all substance was replaced with researched material.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced boilerplate definition, vocabulary, and worked example with researched content on the healthcare workforce, ownership types, and governance.
Added dated workforce statistics (2024) and hospital ownership counts (2024 AHA survey) in place of undated generic prose.
rightsIssues: All sources are U.S. federal government or a trade-association data table used as REFERENCE_ONLY. No source wording was reproduced; figures are facts, and all prose is original. AHA Fast Facts is a copyrighted compilation but the underlying counts are facts cited with attribution and year.
